title.en: Volume 55 Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, F Long
title.raw: 卷五十五 列傳第十五 臧燾 徐廣 傅隆 Volume 55 Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, F Long

sentences.zh: 列傳第十五 臧燾徐廣傅隆

translations.literal: Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, and Fu Long
translations.idiomatic: Biography 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, and Fu Long

sentences.zh: 臧燾，字德仁，東莞莒人，武敬皇后兄也。

translations.literal: Zang Dao, styled Deren, was a native of Ju in Dongguan and elder brother of Empress Dowager Wu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dao, courtesy name Deren, came from Ju in Dongguan and was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wu Jing.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善《三禮》，貧約自立，操行為鄉里所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, excelled in the Three Rites, upheld himself in poverty and frugality, and his conduct was praised in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was devoted to study, mastered the Three Rites, and though poor lived self-reliantly; his character won praise throughout his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元中，衛將軍謝安始立國學，徐、兗二州刺史謝玄舉燾為助教。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Defender-in-Chief Xie An first established the National Academy; Xie Xuan, regional inspector of Xu and Yan, recommended Dao as assistant instructor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taikang reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, when Defender-in-Chief Xie An founded the National Academy, Xie Xuan, governor of Xu and Yan, nominated Dao as an assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝追崇庶祖母宣太后，議者或謂宜配食中宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously honored his father's concubine mother, Empress Dowager Xuan, and some in the deliberations said she should receive offerings in the temple of Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu raised posthumous honors for his father's concubine mother, Empress Dowager Xuan, some advisers argued that she ought to share sacrifices in Emperor Zhongzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 燾議曰：「《陽秋》，之義，母以子貴，故仲子、成風，咸稱夫人。

translations.literal: Dao submitted a memorial saying: "The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that a mother is ennobled through her son; therefore Zhongzi and Cheng Feng were both styled Lady."
translations.idiomatic: Dao argued: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, a mother gains rank through her son—hence Zhongzi and Cheng Feng were both addressed as ladies."

sentences.zh: 《經》雲'考仲子之宮'。

translations.literal: The Classic says, 'He visited the shrine of Zhongzi.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic records that he 'visited the shrine of Zhongzi.'

sentences.zh: 若配食惠廟，則宮無緣別築。

translations.literal: If she were to share offerings in the temple of Emperor Hui, there would be no reason to build a separate shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Were she to share the temple of Emperor Hui, there would be no occasion to erect a separate shrine.

sentences.zh: 前漢孝文、孝昭太后，並系子為號，祭於寢園，不配于高祖、孝武之廟。

translations.literal: In Former Han, the empress dowagers of Emperors Xiaowen and Xiaozhao both took titles derived from their sons, were sacrificed to in the park shrines at the tombs, and did not share the temples of Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Han, the mothers of Emperors Wen and Zhao took titles from their sons, received sacrifice in tomb-garden shrines, and were not enshrined with Gaozu or Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 後漢和帝之母曰恭懷皇所，安帝祖母曰敬隱皇后，順帝之母曰恭湣皇后，雖不系子為號，亦祭於陵寢。

translations.literal: In Later Han, the mother of Emperor He was called Empress Gonghuai, the grandmother of Emperor An was Empress Jingyin, and the mother of Emperor Shun was Empress Gongmin; though their titles were not derived from their sons, they too were sacrificed to at the tomb shrines.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, Emperor He's mother was styled Empress Gonghuai, Emperor An's grandmother Empress Jingyin, and Emperor Shun's mother Empress Gongmin; even without titles tied to their sons, all were honored at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 不配章、安二帝。

translations.literal: They did not share the temples of Emperors Zhang and An.
translations.idiomatic: None of them shared the temples of Emperors Zhang and An.

sentences.zh: 此則二漢雖有太后、皇后之異，至於並不配食，義同《陽秋》。

translations.literal: Thus although the two Han dynasties differed in whether they used the titles empress dowager or empress, in neither case were they given shared temple offerings—the principle matches that of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Thus across both Han dynasties, whatever the difference between empress dowager and empress, none received shared temple sacrifice—a practice in keeping with the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 唯光武追廢呂後，故以薄後配高祖廟。

translations.literal: Only Guangwu, having posthumously deposed Empress Lü, placed Empress Bo in the temple of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Only Emperor Guangwu, having posthumously deposed Empress Lü, installed Empress Bo in Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 又衛後既廢，霍光追尊李夫人為皇后，配孝武廟，此非母以子貴之例，直以高、武二廟無配故耳。

translations.literal: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and placed her in the temple of Emperor Xiaowu; this was not a case of a mother ennobled through her son, but simply because the temples of Gaozu and Wu had no consort to accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously elevated Lady Li to empress and enshrined her with Emperor Wu—a special case, not mother-through-son ennoblement, but because Gaozu's and Wu's temples lacked a consort.

sentences.zh: 夫漢立寢於陵，自是晉制所異。

translations.literal: That Han established shrines at the tombs was itself a practice differing from Jin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Han practice of erecting tomb shrines already differed from Jin ritual.

sentences.zh: 謂宜遠准《陽秋》考宮之義，近摹二漢不配之典。

translations.literal: He held that one should take as distant standard the meaning of visiting the shrine in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and as near model the precedent of the two Han in not granting shared temple offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He urged taking the Spring and Autumn's shrine visit as the distant precedent and the two Han dynasties' refusal of shared sacrifice as the immediate model.

sentences.zh: 尊號既正，則罔極之情申，別建寢廟，則嚴禰之義顯，系子為稱，兼明母貴之所由，一舉而允三義，固哲王之高致也。

translations.literal: Once the honorific title is made correct, boundless filial feeling is expressed; building a separate tomb shrine makes the solemn meaning of ancestral worship clear; taking a title from the son also clarifies the source of a mother's elevation—satisfying three principles at once is indeed the lofty attainment of a sage ruler.
translations.idiomatic: With the proper honorific, filial devotion finds its fullest expression; a separate tomb shrine upholds solemn ancestral worship; a title drawn from the son shows why the mother was ennobled—three rites satisfied at once is the mark of a sage king.

sentences.zh: 」議者從之。

translations.literal: " The deliberators followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 頃之，去官。

translations.literal: Before long he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 以母老家貧，與弟熹俱棄人事，躬耕自業，約己養親者十餘載。

translations.literal: Because his mother was aged and the family poor, he and his younger brother Xi both abandoned public affairs, tilled the fields themselves, restrained themselves and supported their parents for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: With an elderly mother and a poor household, he and his younger brother Xi withdrew from public life, farmed with their own hands, and for more than a decade lived frugally to support their parents.

sentences.zh: 父母喪亡，居喪六年，以毀瘠著稱。

translations.literal: When his parents died he observed mourning for six years and became renowned for emaciating himself in grief.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents' deaths he mourned six years and won fame for wasting away in filial grief.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除臨沂令。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was named magistrate of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，為太學博士，參右將軍何無忌軍事，隨府轉鎮南參軍。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised he became an Erudite of the National Academy, served on the staff of General of the Right He Wuji, and with the headquarters was transferred to staff officer of the Pacification of the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu raised the righteous banner, he became a National Academy erudite, joined General of the Right He Wuji's staff, and later became Pacification of the South staff officer when the command transferred.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮京口，與燾書曰：「頃學尚廢弛，後進頹業，衡門之內，清風輟響。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu was stationed at Jingkou he wrote to Dao: "Recently learning has lain in neglect, the younger generation's studies have collapsed, and within humble doorways the sound of pure conduct has fallen silent."
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Jingkou, the Gaozu wrote to Dao: "Learning has lately fallen into neglect; the younger generation's studies have collapsed, and no clear moral wind stirs behind humble gates."

sentences.zh: 良由戎車屢警，禮樂中息，浮夫恣志，情與事染，豈可不敷崇墳籍，敦厲風尚。

translations.literal: Truly because war-chariots have repeatedly sounded the alarm, rites and music have ceased midway, and drifting men indulge their wills—their feelings stained by affairs—how can we fail to spread esteem for the classics and urge refinement of custom?
translations.idiomatic: War has sounded the alarm again and again; rites and music have stalled; drifting men indulge every whim as feeling and circumstance entangle them—how can we not exalt the classics and stiffen public morals?

sentences.zh: 此境人士，子侄如林，明發搜訪，想聞令軌。

translations.literal: Men of talent in this region, sons and nephews thick as a forest—at dawn I shall search them out and hope to hear of their fine conduct.
translations.idiomatic: This region teems with promising sons and nephews; at daybreak I shall seek them out, eager to hear of their exemplary conduct.

sentences.zh: 然荊玉含寶，要俟開瑩，幽蘭懷馨，事資扇發，獨習寡悟，義著周典。

translations.literal: Yet jade from Jing holds its gem and must await polishing; orchids in the shade bear fragrance and need a fan to spread it—solitary study yields little understanding, as the Zhou classics make clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet jade from Jing hides its luster until cut and polished; orchids in shade keep their fragrance until someone fans it abroad—solitary study rarely enlightens, as the Zhou classics teach.

sentences.zh: 今經師不遠，而赴業無聞，非唯志學者鮮，或是勸誘未至邪。

translations.literal: Now classic masters are not far off, yet no word comes of students coming to study—is it not only that aspirants are few, or perhaps encouragement has not yet reached them?
translations.idiomatic: Classic masters are close at hand, yet no one seems to be enrolling—is it only that few wish to study, or that encouragement has not yet reached them?

sentences.zh: 想複弘之。

translations.literal: I trust you will again broaden this effort.
translations.idiomatic: I trust you will carry this forward once more.

sentences.zh: 」參高祖中軍軍事，入補尚書度支郎，改掌祠部。

translations.literal: " He served on the staff of the Gaozu's Central Army, entered the ministry as a clerk of the Revenue Section, and was transferred to head the Sacrifices Section.
translations.idiomatic: " He joined the Gaozu's Central Army staff, entered the ministry as Revenue Section clerk, then took charge of the Sacrifices Section.

sentences.zh: 襲封高陵亭侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Gaoling district.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Marquis of Gaoling district.

sentences.zh: 時太廟鴟尾災，燾謂著作郎徐廣曰：「昔孔子在齊，聞魯廟災，曰必桓、僖也。

translations.literal: At that time the ridge ornaments of the Imperial Ancestral Temple caught fire; Dao said to Xu Guang, Master of Writings: "In antiquity Confucius, while in Qi, heard that the Lu temple had burned and said it must be Duke Huan and Duke Xi."
translations.idiomatic: When fire struck the temple's ridge ornaments, Dao told Master of Writings Xu Guang: "Confucius once heard from Qi that Lu's temple had burned and said it must concern Dukes Huan and Xi."

sentences.zh: 今征西、京兆四府君，宜在毀落，而猶列廟饗，此其征乎？

translations.literal: Now the four lords of Zhengxi and Jingzhao ought to have been removed from the temples, yet they still stand in the line of sacrifice—is this not the omen?"
translations.idiomatic: Today the four lords of Zhengxi and Jingzhao ought long ago to have been removed, yet they still receive temple sacrifice—is this not the sign?"

sentences.zh: 」乃上議曰：「臣聞國之大事，在祀與戎，將營宮室，宗廟為首。

translations.literal: " He then submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war; when palaces are to be built, the ancestral temple comes first."
translations.idiomatic: " He then memorialized the throne: "I have heard that a state's greatest concerns are sacrifice and war, and that when palaces are planned, the ancestral temple comes first."

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，莫不致肅恭之誠心，盡崇嚴乎祖考，然後能流淳化于四海，通幽感於神明。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity all devoted reverent and sincere hearts and paid fullest honor to their ancestors and fathers; only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and the hidden realm reach the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings of old devoted reverent hearts and fullest honor to their forebears; only then could pure teaching spread across the realm and the hidden world touch the spirits.

sentences.zh: 固宜詳廢興於古典，循情禮以求中者也。

translations.literal: One should indeed examine abolition and establishment in the ancient classics and follow feeling and ritual to seek the mean.
translations.idiomatic: One ought to weigh abolition and establishment against the ancient classics and follow feeling and ritual to the mean.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖而七。

translations.literal: Ritual prescribes seven temples for the Son of Heaven: three zhao and three mu, with the Grand Ancestor making seven.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual assigns the Son of Heaven seven temples—three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor, seven in all.

sentences.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之，遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。

translations.literal: From the temple of one's father back through the five temples to one's great-great-grandfather, all receive monthly sacrifice; distant temples become tiao, and when there are two tiao, seasonal offerings cease.
translations.idiomatic: From the father temple through five generations to the great-great-grandfather, all receive monthly sacrifice; distant temples become tiao, and once there are two tiao, only seasonal offerings remain.

sentences.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之。

translations.literal: Beyond the tiao one makes an altar; beyond the altar a open-air mound; only when there is prayer does one sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the tiao stands an altar; beyond the altar an open mound; sacrifice there only when prayer is required.

sentences.zh: 此宗廟之次，親疏之序也。

translations.literal: This is the order of the ancestral temples and the sequence of closeness and distance in kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the order of ancestral temples and the gradation of kinship near and far.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王、武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan held that the tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held that they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan identified the tiao as the temples of Kings Wen and Wu; Wang Su as ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

sentences.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。

translations.literal: Examining the phrase 'beyond the tiao,' the tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On the phrase 'beyond the tiao,' the tiao cannot mean the temples of Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 文、武周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？

translations.literal: Wen and Wu were the founding ancestors of Zhou—how could one speak of 'beyond the tiao' as making an altar?
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu were Zhou's founding ancestors—how could ritual speak of setting them 'beyond the tiao' at a mere altar?

sentences.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。

translations.literal: This clarifies that distant temples made tiao are ancestors for whom mourning garments are no longer worn.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the tiao are distant ancestors beyond the mourning-garment limit.

sentences.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之禮，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者，其義彌疏也。

translations.literal: Again, distant temples still have seasonal offerings; beyond the tiao there are the distinct altar and mound—showing that the farther the generation, the more attenuated the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Distant temples still receive seasonal offerings; beyond the tiao lie altar and mound—rites grow sparser as generations recede.

sentences.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。

translations.literal: If the tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought to receive monthly sacrifice together with the Grand Ancestor; though Hou Ji was elevated to accompany Heaven in sacrifice, that was because merit and virtue began with him—not that the meaning of honor always admits gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Were the tiao Wen and Wu's temples, they would share monthly sacrifice with the Grand Ancestor; Hou Ji was paired with Heaven because merit began with him—not because honor itself admits endless gradation.

sentences.zh: 又禮有以多貴者，故傳稱德厚者流光，德薄者流卑。

translations.literal: Again, ritual holds that abundance confers honor; hence the tradition says those of thick virtue cast their light far, those of thin virtue cast it low.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual also holds that abundance confers honor; tradition says thick virtue casts light far, thin virtue casts it low.

sentences.zh: 又雲自上以下，降殺以兩，禮也。

translations.literal: It also says that from above downward, diminution proceeds by twos—such is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: It also says honor diminishes by steps of two from above downward—that is ritual.

sentences.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。

translations.literal: This is the canon of noble and base, high and low, and the text of distinction between superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the canon of rank and the rule of distinction between high and low.

sentences.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet to say that Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples—how can that be?
translations.idiomatic: Yet how can Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at only five temples?

sentences.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫，而上祀之禮，不過高祖。

translations.literal: Again, the king sacrifices to legitimate heirs who died young, extending down to remote descendants, yet upward sacrifice does not go beyond the high ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: A king may sacrifice to legitimate heirs who died young, even remote descendants, yet upward sacrifice stops at the high ancestor.

sentences.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊屬，亦非聖人制禮之意也。

translations.literal: Pushing elevated favor down the descending line while displacing sincere reverence toward honored kin is also not the intent of the sages in establishing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Heaping favor on distant descendants while displacing reverence owed to honored forebears was never the sages' intent in ritual.

sentences.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。

translations.literal: Therefore when temples were established in the Taishi era, the court followed the Wang clan's proposal: by ritual the father ranked as a common officer, the son as Son of Heaven or feudal lord; sacrifice was performed as to Son of Heaven or feudal lord, but the impersonator's garment was that of a common officer.
translations.idiomatic: When temples were founded in the Taishi era, the court followed the Wang proposal: ritually the father ranked as a common officer though the son was emperor; sacrifice used imperial rites, but the impersonator wore a commoner's robe.

sentences.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數，宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。

translations.literal: Thus sacrifice extended up to Lord Zhengxi to complete the count of six generations; though Emperor Xuan was Grand Ancestor, he still stood in the place of a descendant, and on the day of the great seasonal sacrifice the rite of facing east was not performed for him—what is called 'though the son equals the sage, he does not eat before his father.'
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice therefore reached Lord Zhengxi to fill six generations; though Emperor Xuan was Grand Ancestor, he still ranked as a descendant, and on the great seasonal day he received no east-facing rite—'though the son equals a sage, he does not eat before his father.'

sentences.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨。

translations.literal: Now that those above Jingzhao have been removed, the Grand Ancestor can at last take the central place; deliberators, holding that zhao and mu are not yet complete, wish to place the Grand Ancestor in a lower seat—your servant holds this contrary to the intent of the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Jingzhao line has been removed, the Grand Ancestor can take the central seat; some argue zhao and mu are incomplete and would demote him—your servant finds that contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 所與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太祖在六世之外，非為須滿七廟，乃得居太祖也。

translations.literal: 'Seven together with the Grand Ancestor' means zhao and mu are already complete; the Grand Ancestor stands outside the six generations—it is not that one must fill seven temples before he may occupy the place of Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: 'Seven with the Grand Ancestor' means zhao and mu are already sufficient; the Grand Ancestor stands beyond the six generations—not that seven temples must be filled before he takes his place.

sentences.zh: 議者又以四府君神主宜永同于殷祫，臣又以為不然。

translations.literal: Deliberators also held that the spirit tablets of the four lords ought forever to share the great seasonal sacrifice—your servant again disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: Others argued the four lords' tablets should forever share the great seasonal sacrifice—your servant again disagreed.

sentences.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。

translations.literal: What the tradition calls 'the tablets of demolished temples are displayed before the Grand Ancestor' means the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When tradition says demolished temples' tablets are set before the Grand Ancestor, it means former lords below him—not above.

sentences.zh: 故《白虎通》雲'禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。

translations.literal: Hence the Baihu tong says: 'The great seasonal sacrifices to removed temples are because they embody succession to the lordship and maintain the line without break.'
translations.idiomatic: The Baihu tong explains: 'Great seasonal sacrifice to removed temples honors those who embodied succession and kept the line unbroken.'

sentences.zh: 」豈如四府君在太祖之前乎。

translations.literal: " How could the four lords stand before the Grand Ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: " How could the four lords rank before the Grand Ancestor?

sentences.zh: 非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基，昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍，未見其可。

translations.literal: They were not lords who inherited the succession, bore no auspicious mandate of the spirits, and were not the foundation of royal enterprise; formerly they were included because the generation was near, but now feeling and ritual are far removed—yet they would forever share the great seasonal sacrifice and permanently leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; searching the ritual records, one does not find this permissible.
translations.idiomatic: They did not inherit the throne, bore no mandate from Heaven, and laid no foundation for the dynasty; they were honored once because the generation was near, but feeling and ritual have long since receded—yet they would forever share the great sacrifice and leave the Grand Ancestor's seat empty; the ritual books offer no warrant.

sentences.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以淵儒碩學，鹹謂四府君神主，無緣永存於百世。

translations.literal: In the early Yonghe era this ritual was debated at length; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound scholars, all held that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no grounds to endure for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yonghe the court debated this at length; Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, leading scholars both, agreed the four lords' tablets could not endure for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所秉小異，而大歸是同。

translations.literal: Some wished to bury them between the steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them—though their particular views differed slightly, the main conclusion was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed burying them between the steps, others storing them in a stone chamber, others rebuilding shrines—minor differences, but the conclusion was the same.

sentences.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭，長無太祖之位矣。

translations.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the mass of temples while the four lords' great seasonal sacrifices never cease, then in Great Jin's great seasonal rites the Grand Ancestor's place would long remain vacant.
translations.idiomatic: If Emperor Xuan already towers above the other temples while the four lords forever share the great sacrifice, Jin's seasonal rites would forever lack a seat for the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚；

translations.literal: Principle values the mean and need not be excessive;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual values the mean and need not run to excess;

sentences.zh: 禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷！

translations.literal: ritual shifts with the age—how can one follow it without also cutting off what is due?
translations.idiomatic: ritual shifts with the times—how can one follow custom without also knowing when to end it?

sentences.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈厲之諡彌彰；

translations.literal: thus though a subject's feeling may be deep, the posthumous title of spiritual severity becomes all the more manifest;
translations.idiomatic: Thus though a subject's devotion may run deep, posthumous titles of spiritual austerity grow all the clearer;

sentences.zh: 追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。

translations.literal: though longing for the distant past may be keen, the rite of transfer and demolition is what applies.
translations.idiomatic: though longing for the distant dead may be keen, the rites of transfer and demolition must prevail.

sentences.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可逾爾。

translations.literal: Is it not that one has the heart to add further honor, yet ritual institutions cannot be transgressed?
translations.idiomatic: One may wish to heap further honor, yet ritual cannot be overstepped.

sentences.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處，虞主所以依神，神移則有 瘞埋之禮。

translations.literal: A stone chamber would store them north of the temple; rebuilding would leave their location uncertain; the temporary lord-tablet exists to lodge the spirit—when the spirit moves, there is the rite of burial in the earth.
translations.idiomatic: A stone chamber would lie north of the temple; rebuilding would leave their site uncertain; the temporary tablet lodges the spirit, and when the spirit departs, burial rites apply.

sentences.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也，准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。

translations.literal: If sacrifice to the four lords ought to be abolished, their spirits likewise have nothing to lodge in; following parallel precedents, they should be buried like temporary lord-tablets.
translations.idiomatic: If sacrifice to the four lords should cease, their spirits have no further dwelling; by precedent they should be buried like temporary tablets.

sentences.zh: 然經典難詳，群言紛錯，非臣卑淺所能折中。

translations.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail fully and many opinions tangle—this is not something your servant's shallow station can reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the classics are obscure and opinions tangle—more than your servant's shallow learning can reconcile.

sentences.zh: 」時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。

translations.literal: " At the time many scholars followed Dao's proposal, but in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Many scholars then sided with Dao, but in the end his proposal was never enacted.

sentences.zh: 遷通直郎，高祖鎮軍、車騎、中軍、太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant of Direct Communication and served the Gaozu as advisory staff officer to the Pacifying Army, Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army, and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Palace Attendant of Direct Communication, he served the Gaozu as advisory staff officer under the Pacifying Army, Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army, and Grand Marshal commands.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐關、洛，大司馬琅邪王同行，除大司馬從事中郎，總留府事。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu marched north against Guan and Luo, the Prince of Langye, Grand Marshal, accompanied him; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman of the Grand Marshal and oversaw all affairs left at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the Gaozu's northern campaign toward Guan and Luo, the Prince of Langye marched as Grand Marshal; Dao was named attendant gentleman of the Grand Marshal and directed all affairs left behind at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 義熙十四年，除侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元熙元年，以腳疾去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi he left office because of foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxi he resigned because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，征拜太常，雖外戚貴顯，而彌自沖約，茅屋蔬餐，不改其舊。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu received the Mandate he was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies; though a prominent maternal relative, he became all the more self-restrained and modest, keeping his thatched hut and vegetable meals unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu took the throne he was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies; though now a powerful imperial in-law, he grew only more modest, living still in his thatched hut on plain vegetables.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿，與親戚共之。

translations.literal: The salary he received he shared with kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He shared his salary with his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，致仕，拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he retired, receiving the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，時年七十。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year, at seventy.

sentences.zh: 少帝追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor posthumously honored him as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and added the title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor posthumously honored him as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 長子邃，護軍司馬，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Sui was staff officer of the Protector Army and governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Sui served as staff officer of the Protector Army and governor of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 少子綽，太子中舍人，新安太守。

translations.literal: His younger son Chuo was attendant in the Crown Prince's palace and governor of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Chuo was attendant in the Crown Prince's household and governor of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 邃長子諶之，尚書都官郎，烏程令。

translations.literal: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi was a clerk in the Ministry of Works' Punishments Section and magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi served as a clerk in the Ministry of Works' Punishments Section and as magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 諶之弟凝之，學涉有當世才具，與司空徐湛之為異常之交。

translations.literal: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was broadly learned and possessed talent for his age; with Minister of Works Xu Tanzhi he formed an extraordinary friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was widely learned and gifted for his generation; he formed an unusually close bond with Minister of Works Xu Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 年少時與北地傅僧祐俱以通家子始為太祖所引見，時上與何尚之論鑄錢事，凝之便幹其語，上因回與論之。

translations.literal: In youth, together with Fu Sengyou of Beidi, he was first introduced to the Gaozu as sons of allied families; at the time the emperor was discussing coinage with He Shangzhi, and Ningzhi at once joined their conversation, whereupon the emperor turned and debated with him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Fu Sengyou of Beidi, as sons of allied families, were first presented to the Gaozu; while the emperor debated coinage with He Shangzhi, Ningzhi broke in, and the emperor turned to argue with him.

sentences.zh: 僧祐引凝之衣令止，凝之大言謂僧祐曰：「明主難再遇，便應正盡所懷。

translations.literal: Sengyou pulled Ningzhi's robe to make him stop; Ningzhi spoke loudly to Sengyou: "A clear-sighted ruler is hard to meet twice—one ought at once to set forth one's mind fully."
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou tugged his robe to silence him; Ningzhi said loudly: "A wise ruler is rarely met twice—we should speak our minds plainly now."

sentences.zh: 」上與往復十餘反，凝之詞韻銓序，兼有理證，上甚賞焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor and he went back and forth more than ten rounds; Ningzhi's words were measured in tone and orderly, with reasoning and evidence together, and the emperor greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: " They exchanged more than ten rounds; Ningzhi spoke with measured eloquence and sound argument, and the emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 曆隨王誕後軍記室錄事，欲以為青州，其事不果。

translations.literal: He served successively as recorder-clerk on the staff of Prince Dan of Sui's Rear Army; there was a plan to make him regional inspector of Qingzhou, but it did not come about.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder on Prince Dan of Sui's Rear Army staff; a plan to appoint him governor of Qingzhou came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞，以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Ministry of Works; as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi he was killed by the prime culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Ministry of Works, he was killed as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi in the prince's revolt.

sentences.zh: 子夤，尚書主客郎，沈攸之征西功曹，為攸之盡節，事在《攸之傳》。

translations.literal: His son Yin was a clerk in the Ministry of Works' Guests Section and staff officer of Pacification of the West under Shen Youzhi; he gave his utmost loyalty to Youzhi—the account is in the biography of Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin served as Guests Section clerk and Pacification of the West staff officer under Shen Youzhi, dying in loyal service to him, as told in Youzhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 凝之弟潭之，亦有美譽。

translations.literal: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi also enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi likewise enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，曆尚書吏部郎，禦史中丞。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Taizong he served successively as director of the Ministry of Works' Personnel Section and Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he served as director of the Personnel Section and as Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，為左民尚書，卒官。

translations.literal: Under the Later Deposed Emperor, in the Yuanhui era, he was Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Deposed Emperor, in the Yuanhui era, he served as Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.

sentences.zh: 潭之弟澄之，太子左積弩將軍。

translations.literal: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi was Left Commander of Stacked Crossbows in the Crown Prince's guard.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi was Left Commander of Stacked Crossbows in the Crown Prince's guard.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，領軍於盱眙，為索虜所破，見殺，追贈通直郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded troops at Xuyi, was defeated by the northern barbarians, and was killed; posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded at Xuyi, was routed by the northern enemy, and killed; posthumously he received the title Palace Attendant of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 綽子煥，順帝升明中，為武昌太守。

translations.literal: Chuo's son Huan, in the Shengming era of Emperor Shun, was governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's son Huan served as governor of Wuchang in the Shengming era of Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之攻郢城，煥棄郡赴之；

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi attacked Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his commandery and went to join him;
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi besieged Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his post and rushed to join him;

sentences.zh: 攸之敗，伏誅。

translations.literal: when Youzhi was defeated, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: when Youzhi fell, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 傅僧祐，祖父弘仁，高祖外弟也。

translations.literal: Fu Sengyou's grandfather Hongren was a younger brother of the Gaozu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sengyou's grandfather Hongren was a maternal younger brother of the Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 以中表曆顯官，征虜將軍、南譙太守，太常卿。

translations.literal: Through maternal kin connections he rose through prominent offices: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Through ties of maternal kinship he rose to high office, serving as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 子邵，員外散騎侍郎，妻燾女也，生僧祐，有吏才，再為山陰令，甚有能名，末世令長莫及。

translations.literal: His son Shao was an attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; he married Dao's daughter and fathered Sengyou, who had talent for administration, twice served as magistrate of Shanyin, enjoyed a great reputation for competence, and at the end of the dynasty no district magistrate could match him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao was an attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; he married Dao's daughter and fathered Sengyou, a capable administrator who twice governed Shanyin and won such a reputation that no magistrate of the late dynasty could rival him.

sentences.zh: 亦以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: He too, as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi, was killed by the prime culprit.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi in the prince's revolt.

sentences.zh: 徐廣，字野民，東莞姑幕人也。

translations.literal: Xu Guang, styled Yemin, was a native of Gumu in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang, courtesy name Yemin, came from Gumu in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 父藻，都水使者。

translations.literal: His father Zao was Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao served as Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 兄邈，太子前衛率。

translations.literal: His elder brother Miao was commander of the Crown Prince's Forward Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Miao commanded the Crown Prince's Forward Guard.

sentences.zh: 家世好學，至廣尤精，百家數術，無不研覽。

translations.literal: His family for generations loved learning; Guang in particular was most accomplished, and among the hundred schools and numerological arts there was none he did not study.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long prized learning; Guang surpassed them all, mastering every school of thought and art of calculation the classics record.

sentences.zh: 謝玄為州，辟廣從事西曹。

translations.literal: When Xie Xuan was regional inspector, he summoned Guang as Western Bureau staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Xuan governed the province, he recruited Guang as Western Bureau staff officer.

sentences.zh: 又譙王司馬恬鎮北參軍。

translations.literal: He also served Prince Qiao, Sima Tian, as staff officer of the Pacification of the North.
translations.idiomatic: He also served Prince Qiao, Sima Tian, as Pacification of the North staff officer.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝以廣博學，除為秘書郎，校書秘閣，增置職僚。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, because of Guang's broad learning, appointed him Secretary Gentleman to collate books in the Secret Archive and added staff positions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, impressed by Guang's erudition, named him Secretary Gentleman to collate texts in the Secret Archive and expanded the staff.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎，領校書如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry outside the regular roster, continuing to oversee collation as before.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, he continued to oversee collation as before.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，尚書令王珣舉為祠部郎。

translations.literal: In the Longan era, Minister of Works Wang Xun recommended him as clerk of the Sacrifices Section.
translations.idiomatic: During Longan, Minister of Works Wang Xun recommended him as Sacrifices Section clerk.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王世子元顯錄尚書，欲使百僚致敬，台內使廣立議，由是內外並執下官禮，廣常為愧恨焉。

translations.literal: At the time the heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, Yuan Xian, recorded affairs of the Ministry of Works and wished to make all officials pay homage; within the ministry Guang was made to draft the proposal, whereupon inside and outside alike observed the ceremony for inferiors—Guang was often ashamed and resentful of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuaiji's heir Yuan Xian took charge of the ministry and demanded homage from all officials, Guang was ordered to draft the protocol; court and provinces alike then observed inferior-to-superior rites—a source of lasting shame and resentment for Guang.

sentences.zh: 元顯引為中軍參軍，遷領軍長史。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian brought him in as staff officer of the Central Army and promoted him to chief clerk of the Commandant Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian recruited him as Central Army staff officer, then made him chief clerk of the Commandant Army.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，以為大將軍文學祭酒。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted in government, he was appointed libationer of letters for the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan Xuan's regency he became libationer of letters on the Grand Marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，高祖使撰車服儀注，乃除鎮軍諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: In early Yixi the Gaozu had him compile regulations for carriages, robes, and ceremonial observances, and appointed him advisory staff officer of the Pacifying Army, heading the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yixi the Gaozu commissioned him to draft regulations for carriages, dress, and court ceremony, naming him advisory staff officer of the Pacifying Army and head of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 封樂成縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Lecheng district.
translations.idiomatic: He received the fifth-rank marquisate of Lecheng district.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎常侍，領著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regular attendant of the Scattered Cavalry outside the roster and headed the Bureau of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to regular attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, he headed the Bureau of Writings.

sentences.zh: 二年，尚書奏曰：「臣聞左史述言，右官書事，《乘》、《志》顯于晉、鄭，《陽秋》著乎魯史。

translations.literal: In the second year the Ministry of Works memorialized: "Your servants have heard that the left historiographer records words and the right officer records affairs; the Cheng and Zhi shone forth in Jin and Zheng, the Spring and Autumn Annals were set down in Lu's chronicle."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the ministry memorialized: "We have heard that the left historiographer records speech and the right officer records events; the Cheng and Zhi made their mark in Jin and Zheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were written in Lu's chronicle."

sentences.zh: 自皇代有造，中興晉祀，道風帝典，煥乎史策。

translations.literal: Since the imperial age was founded and the Jin sacrifices were restored, the Way, customs, and imperial canons have blazed forth in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty was founded and Jin ritual was restored, the Way, imperial custom, and sage precedent have shone bright in the annals.

sentences.zh: 而太和以降，世曆三朝，玄風聖跡，倏為疇古。

translations.literal: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed, and the subtle wind and sage traces have suddenly become antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Taihe reign three dynasties have passed, and the subtle ethos and traces of sages have already turned to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳，宜敕著作郎徐廣撰成國史。

translations.literal: Your servants have examined the matter and hold that Xu Guang, Master of Writings, should be ordered to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: We recommend that Master of Writings Xu Guang be ordered to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「先朝至德光被，未著方策，宜流風緬代，永貽將來者也。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "The utmost virtue of the former court shines abroad yet is not set down in the records; its flowing influence should be extended through generations and bequeathed forever to those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "The former court's supreme virtue shines abroad yet remains unwritten; its influence should flow down the ages and be left as a lasting gift to posterity."

sentences.zh: 便敕撰集。」

translations.literal: Let compilation be ordered at once."
translations.idiomatic: Begin the compilation at once."

sentences.zh: 六年，遷散騎常侍，又領徐州大中正，轉正員常侍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to regular attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, also headed the great impartial judge of Xuzhou, and was transferred to regular attendant on the regular roster.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became regular attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, also served as great impartial judge of Xuzhou, and then took a regular roster post as attendant.

sentences.zh: 時有風雹為災，廣獻書高祖曰：「風雹變未必為災，古之聖賢輒懼而修己，所以興政化而隆德教也。

translations.literal: At the time wind and hail brought disaster; Guang submitted a letter to the Gaozu saying: "Wind and hail need not be calamities; the sages of old at once feared them and cultivated themselves—thereby raising government and exalting moral teaching."
translations.idiomatic: When wind and hail brought disaster, Guang wrote the Gaozu: "Such omens need not spell calamity; sage kings of old took them as warnings to refine themselves—thereby advancing government and elevating moral teaching."

sentences.zh: 嘗忝服事，宿眷未忘，思竭塵露，率誠于習。

translations.literal: I once had the honor to serve you; old favor is not forgotten; I wish to exhaust my trifling strength and offer sincerity in what I have learned.
translations.idiomatic: I once had the honor to serve you and have not forgotten that old favor; I offer what little strength I have in sincere counsel drawn from long habit.

sentences.zh: 明公初建義旗，匡複宗社，神武應運，信宿平夷。

translations.literal: When my lord first raised the righteous banner, restored the altars of state, and with divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, within a night and a day peace was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: When you first raised the righteous banner and restored the altars of state, your divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, and within a day and night the realm was pacified.

sentences.zh: 且恭儉謙約，虛心匪懈，來蘇之化，功用若神。

translations.literal: Moreover you are respectful, frugal, modest, and restrained, with an untiring open mind; the transformation that brings renewal works as if by spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you are respectful, frugal, and modest, never slack in self-cultivation; the renewal you bring works almost like a divine gift.

sentences.zh: 頃事故既多，刑德並用，戰功殷積，報敘難盡，萬機繁湊，固應難速，且小細煩密，群下多懼。

translations.literal: Recently affairs have been many, punishment and virtue employed together, battle merit heaped up and rewards hard to exhaust, the myriad tasks dense and pressing—it is naturally hard to be swift; moreover petty matters are intricate and subordinates are much afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Lately affairs have multiplied; punishment and grace are applied together; battle honors pile up faster than rewards can be granted; the myriad tasks are dense—it is naturally hard to move quickly, and petty regulations leave many below in fear.

sentences.zh: 又谷帛豐賤，而民情不勸；

translations.literal: again grain and cloth are abundant and cheap, yet the people's hearts are not encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: Grain and cloth are plentiful and cheap, yet the people are not stirred to industry;

sentences.zh: 禁司互設，而劫盜多有，誠由俗弊未易整，而望深未易炳。

translations.literal: prohibitory offices are set up in mutual layers yet robbery is frequent—truly because popular abuses are not easily rectified and deep expectations are not easily made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: prohibitory offices multiply yet banditry remains common—truly because deep-rooted custom is hard to reform and high expectations are hard to make clear at once.

sentences.zh: 追思義熙之始，如有不同，何者？

translations.literal: Reflecting on the beginning of Yixi, if there is a difference, what is it?
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to the start of Yixi, if things differ now, wherein lies the change?

sentences.zh: 好安願逸，萬物之大趣，習舊駭新，凡識所不免。

translations.literal: Love of rest and wish for ease are the great bent of all things; habit of the old and shock at the new are what every understanding cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Love of ease is the bent of all living things; shock at the new while clinging to the old is what no mind entirely escapes.

sentences.zh: 要當俯順群情，抑揚隨俗，則朝野歡泰，具瞻允康矣。

translations.literal: One must bow to the feelings of the multitude and moderate according to custom; then court and countryside will rejoice and all eyes will find true peace.
translations.idiomatic: You must bend to popular feeling and moderate policy to custom; then court and countryside will rejoice and all will find true peace.

sentences.zh: 言無可采，願矜其愚款之志。

translations.literal: My words are not worth adopting; I beg you to pity my sincere but foolish intent.
translations.idiomatic: My words may be unworthy of adoption; I beg you to pity my sincere but foolish intent."

sentences.zh: 」又轉大司農，領著作郎皆如故。

translations.literal: " He was again transferred to Minister of the Grand Granary, continuing to head the Bureau of Writings as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Minister of the Grand Granary while continuing to head the Bureau of Writings.

sentences.zh: 十二年，《晉紀》成，凡四十六卷，表上之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Jin Annals were completed, forty-six scrolls in all, and presented in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he completed the Jin Annals in forty-six scrolls and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，桓玄篡位，安帝出宮，廣陪列悲慟，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An left the palace, Guang in the entourage grieved and wept, his sorrow moving those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An was driven from the palace, Guang wept among the attendants until all beside him were moved.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，恭帝遜位，廣又哀感，涕泗交流。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu received the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang again was moved to grief, tears and mucus streaming together.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu received the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang wept again until tears and mucus streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 謝晦見之，謂之曰：「徐公將無小過？

translations.literal: Xie Hui saw this and said to him: "Master Xu, are you not going a little too far?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui saw this and said, "Master Xu, are you not carrying this a bit too far?"

sentences.zh: 」廣收淚答曰：「身與君不同。

translations.literal: " Guang wiped away his tears and answered: "My person and yours are not the same."
translations.idiomatic: " Guang wiped away his tears and replied, "You and I are not in the same position."

sentences.zh: 君佐命興王，逢千載嘉運；

translations.literal: You assisted the Mandate and raised the king, meeting a thousand-year auspicious fortune;
translations.idiomatic: You aided the Mandate and helped raise a new dynasty, meeting a once-in-a-thousand-years fortune;

sentences.zh: 身世荷晉德，實眷戀故主。

translations.literal: my person and life have received Jin's grace and truly still cherish the former sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: my life has received Jin's grace, and I truly still cherish my former lord."

sentences.zh: 」因更歔欷。

translations.literal: " He then sobbed again.
translations.idiomatic: " He sobbed again.

sentences.zh: 傅隆，字伯祚，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Long, styled Bozuo, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Long, courtesy name Bozuo, came from Lingzhou in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 高祖咸，晉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xian was Metropolitan Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xian served as Metropolitan Commandant under Jin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖晞，司徒屬。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xi was an aide in the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xi was an aide in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 父祖早亡。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father and grandfather died while he was young.

sentences.zh: 隆少孤，又無近屬，單貧有學行，不好交遊。

translations.literal: Long was orphaned in youth and had no close kin; alone and poor, he possessed learning and conduct and did not care for socializing.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and without close kin, Long was poor but learned and upright, and cared little for society.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，年四十，始為孟昶建威將軍，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In early Yixi, at forty, he first served Meng Chang as attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry outside the roster under the Pacifying Army general.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yixi, at forty, he first entered service under Meng Chang as attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry on the Pacifying Army staff.

sentences.zh: 坐辭兼，免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for declining a concurrent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed for declining a concurrent post.

sentences.zh: 複為會稽征虜參軍。

translations.literal: He again served as staff officer of the Pacification of the Barbarians in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Pacification of the Barbarians staff officer in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 家在上虞，及東歸，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: His family was in Shangyu; when he returned east he formed the wish to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived in Shangyu; on returning east he resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 曆佐三軍，首尾八年。

translations.literal: He served successively on three armies' staffs, eight years from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: He served on three armies' staffs over eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 除給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射、丹陽尹徐羨之置建威府，以為錄事參軍，尋轉尚書祠部郎、丹陽丞，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works and governor of Danyang Xu Xianzhi established a Pacifying Army headquarters and made him recorder staff officer; soon he was transferred to Sacrifices Section clerk and assistant magistrate of Danyang, then entered the ministry as Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xu Xianzhi, also governor of Danyang, made him recorder on the Pacifying Army staff; he soon became Sacrifices Section clerk and Danyang assistant magistrate, then Left Assistant Director of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 以族弟亮為僕射，緦服不得相臨，徙太子率更令，廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍，出補山陰令。

translations.literal: Because his clansman younger brother Liang was vice minister, as they were in the same degree of mourning garments they could not face each other in office; he was moved to Director of the Crown Prince's Astronomy Office, then advisory staff officer of Chariots and Cavalry to Prince Yizhen of Luling, and went out to fill the post of magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: When his kinsman Liang became vice minister, mourning protocol barred them from serving together; Long was transferred to the Crown Prince's Astronomy Office, then to Prince Yizhen of Luling's staff, and finally went out as magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉初，除司徒右長史，遷禦史中丞。

translations.literal: In early Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education and promoted to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu he became Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education, then Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 當官而行，甚得司直之體。

translations.literal: He acted according to office and fully embodied the integrity of an impartial judge.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law as his office required and fully embodied impartial integrity.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 時會稽剡縣民黃初妻趙打息載妻王死亡，遇赦，王有父母及息男稱、息女葉，依法徙趙二千裏外。

translations.literal: At the time in Yan district of Kuaiji, the wife Zhao of the commoner Huang Chu beat to death the wife Wang of her stepson Zai; an amnesty was granted; Wang had parents and a son Cheng and daughter Ye by a former marriage; by law Zhao was to be exiled two thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan district of Kuaiji, Huang Chu's wife Zhao beat to death the wife Wang of her stepson Zai; though an amnesty followed, Wang's parents and her children Cheng and Ye remained; by law Zhao was to be exiled two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 隆議之曰：「原夫禮律之興，蓋本之自然，求之情理，非從天墮，非從地出也。

translations.literal: Long deliberated on the case, saying: "Tracing the rise of ritual and law, it is rooted in the natural, sought in reason and feeling—it did not fall from Heaven or spring from Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Long ruled on the case: "Ritual and law arise from what is natural and are grounded in reason—they did not fall from Heaven or spring from Earth."

sentences.zh: 父子至親，分形同氣，稱之於載，即載之于趙，雖雲三世，為體猶一，未有能分之者也。

translations.literal: Father and son are utmost kin, sharing form and breath; Cheng to Zai is what Zai is to Zhao—though called three generations, as one body they cannot be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son are the closest kin, sharing flesh and breath; Cheng stands to Zai as Zai stands to Zhao—though three generations are named, they are one body and cannot be split.

sentences.zh: 稱雖創巨痛深，固無仇祖之義。

translations.literal: Though Cheng suffers grievous wound and deep pain, there is surely no principle of avenging a grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cheng's wound is grievous, there is no principle by which he may avenge a grandmother.

sentences.zh: 若稱可以殺趙，趙當何以處載？

translations.literal: If Cheng may kill Zhao, how should Zhao treat Zai?
translations.idiomatic: If Cheng may kill Zhao, what may Zhao do to Zai?

sentences.zh: 將父子孫祖，互相殘戮，懼非先王明罰，咎繇立法之本旨也。

translations.literal: To have father, son, grandson, and grandmother mutually slaughter one another—I fear this is not the intent of the former kings in clarifying punishments and of Gao Yao in establishing law.
translations.idiomatic: Father, son, grandson, and grandmother slaughtering one another—this cannot be what the sage kings intended in clarifying punishments or what Gao Yao intended in framing law.

sentences.zh: 向使石厚之子、日磾之孫，砥鋒挺鍔，不與二祖同戴天日，則石碏、秺侯何得流名百代，以為美談者哉！

translations.literal: Suppose the son of Shi Hou and the grandson of Rizhu had whetted blades and drawn swords and did not share Heaven and sun with their two ancestors—how could Shi Que and the Marquis of Di have left their names for a hundred generations as subjects of praise!
translations.idiomatic: Had the son of Shi Hou and the grandson of Rizhu sharpened blades and refused to live under the same Heaven as their forebears, how could Shi Que and the Marquis of Di be praised for a hundred generations!

sentences.zh: 舊令雲，'殺人父母，徙之二千裏外'。

translations.literal: The old ordinance says: 'Those who kill another's parents are exiled two thousand li away.'
translations.idiomatic: The old ordinance says: 'Whoever kills another's parents is exiled two thousand li.'

sentences.zh: 不施父子孫祖明矣。

translations.literal: That it is not applied to father, son, grandson, and grandmother is clear.
translations.idiomatic: That it does not apply across father, son, grandson, and grandmother is clear.

sentences.zh: 趙當避王期功千里外耳。

translations.literal: Zhao need only avoid Wang's parents and those in the one-year and nine-month mourning grades for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao need only keep a thousand li from Wang's parents and close kin in mourning.

sentences.zh: 令亦雲，'凡流徙者，同籍親近欲相隨者，聽之'。

translations.literal: The ordinance also says: 'For all who are exiled, if close kin of the same registry wish to follow, they are permitted.'
translations.idiomatic: The ordinance also says: 'When anyone is exiled, close kin of the same registry who wish to accompany him may do so.'

sentences.zh: 此又大通情體，因親以教愛者也。

translations.literal: This again broadly accords with feeling and principle, teaching love through kinship.
translations.idiomatic: This too accords with human feeling, teaching love through kinship.

sentences.zh: 趙既流移，載為人子，何得不從；

translations.literal: Since Zhao is exiled, as a son how can Zai fail to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao is exiled; as her son, how can Zai fail to follow;

sentences.zh: 載從而稱不行，豈名教所許？

translations.literal: if Zai follows yet Cheng does not, is that permitted by the teaching of names?
translations.idiomatic: if Zai follows but Cheng does not, can ritual teaching permit it?

sentences.zh: 如此，稱、趙竟不可分。

translations.literal: Thus Cheng and Zhao in the end cannot be separated.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Cheng and Zhao cannot in the end be separated.

sentences.zh: 趙雖內愧終身，稱當沈痛沒齒，孫祖之義，自不得永絕，事理固然也。

translations.literal: Though Zhao may feel inner shame all her life, Cheng should grieve to his grave; the bond of grandson and grandmother cannot be forever severed—such is the logic of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao may bear lifelong shame, and Cheng lifelong grief, but the bond of grandson and grandmother cannot be severed forever—that is the logic of the case."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted his ruling.

sentences.zh: 又出為義興太守，在郡有能名。

translations.literal: He again went out as governor of Yixing and in the commandery enjoyed a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He went out again as governor of Yixing and won a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 征拜左民尚書，坐正直受節假，對人未至，委出，白衣領職。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of the Left for the People; because in uprightness he accepted leave but left his post before the person he was to meet arrived, he was dismissed and served in plain robes while retaining office.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Minister of the Left for the People, he was demoted to plain-robed service for leaving his post during approved leave before an expected visitor arrived.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太常。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太祖以新撰《禮論》付隆使下意，隆上表曰：「臣以下愚，不涉師訓，孤陋閭閻，面牆靡識，謬蒙詢逮，愧懼流汗。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Taizu entrusted Long with the newly compiled Treatise on Rites to obtain his views; Long submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant is low and foolish, has not received teachers' instruction, is solitary and crude in the lanes, faces the wall without knowledge, and has wrongly been questioned—ashamed and afraid, sweating in fear."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Taizu asked Long to review the newly compiled Treatise on Rites; Long memorialized: "I am low and unlearned, without teachers' guidance, crude and isolated, ignorant as one facing a wall—yet I have been questioned and sweat with shame and fear."

sentences.zh: 原夫禮者，三千之本，人倫之至道。

translations.literal: Tracing it, ritual is the root of the three thousand norms and the utmost Way of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is the root of the three thousand norms and the highest Way of human relations.

sentences.zh: 故用之家國，君臣以之尊，父子以之親；

translations.literal: Therefore in state and family, lord and minister through it gain honor, father and son through it gain closeness;
translations.idiomatic: In state and family, lord and minister gain honor through it, father and son gain closeness through it;

sentences.zh: 用之婚冠，少長以之仁愛，夫妻以之義順；

translations.literal: in marriage and capping, young and old through it gain loving kindness, husband and wife through it gain righteous harmony;
translations.idiomatic: in marriage and capping, young and old gain affection through it, husband and wife gain righteous harmony through it;

sentences.zh: 用之鄉人，友朋以之三益，賓主以之敬讓。

translations.literal: in village relations, friends and companions through it gain the three benefits, guest and host through it gain respect and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: among neighbors, friends gain the three benefits through it, guest and host gain respect and yielding through it.

sentences.zh: 所謂極乎天，播乎地，窮高遠，測深厚，莫尚於禮也。

translations.literal: What is called reaching to Heaven, spreading over Earth, exhausting height and distance, measuring depth and thickness—nothing is higher than ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching to Heaven, spreading over Earth, exhausting height and distance, sounding depth and thickness—nothing surpasses ritual.

sentences.zh: 其樂之五聲，《易》之八象，《詩》之《風雅》，《書》之《典誥》，《春秋》之微婉勸懲，無不本乎禮而後立也。

translations.literal: The five tones of Music, the eight images of the Changes, the Airs and Eulogies of the Odes, the Canons and Charges of the Documents, the subtle admonitions and warnings of the Spring and Autumn—all without exception take ritual as root before they can stand.
translations.idiomatic: Music's five tones, the Changes' eight images, the Odes' Airs and Eulogies, the Documents' Canons and Charges, the Spring and Autumn's subtle warnings—all rest on ritual before they can stand.

sentences.zh: 其源遠，其流廣，其體大，其義精，非夫睿哲大賢，孰能明乎此哉。

translations.literal: Its source is far, its flow broad, its body great, its meaning refined—if not a sage of penetrating wisdom, who can clarify this?
translations.idiomatic: Its source is distant, its flow broad, its body vast, its meaning refined—who but a sage of penetrating wisdom can fully grasp it?

sentences.zh: 況遭暴秦焚亡，百不存一。

translations.literal: Moreover it suffered the violent Qin's burning and extinction, so that not one in a hundred remains.
translations.idiomatic: Then came violent Qin's burning, and scarcely one part in a hundred survived.

sentences.zh: 漢興，始徵召故老，搜集殘文，其體例紕繆，首尾脫落，難可詳論。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it first summoned old scholars and gathered remnant texts; their categories were tangled and beginnings and ends missing, hard to discuss in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, old scholars were summoned and remnant texts gathered, but categories were tangled and beginnings and ends lost—hard to discuss in full.

sentences.zh: 幸高堂生頗識舊義，諸儒各為章句之說，既明不獨達，所見不同，或師資相傳，共枝別幹。

translations.literal: Fortunately Master Gaotang knew the old meanings fairly well; the various Confucians each made chapter-and-verse explanations—since understanding was not attained alone, views differed, or teachers and pupils transmitted separately, one trunk with diverging branches.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Gaotang knew the old meanings fairly well; each scholar wrote chapter-and-verse glosses—understanding was not uniform, views diverged, and schools split like branches from one trunk.

sentences.zh: 故聞人、二戴，俱事後蒼，俄已分異；

translations.literal: thus Wenren and the two Dai, all studying under Hou Cang, soon diverged;
translations.idiomatic: Wenren and the two Dai all studied under Hou Cang, yet soon diverged;

sentences.zh: 盧植、鄭玄，偕學馬融，人各名象。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan together studied under Ma Rong, each man with his own terminology.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan both studied under Ma Rong, each with his own terminology.

sentences.zh: 又後之學者，未逮曩時，而問難星繁，充斥兼兩，摛文列錦，煥爛可觀。

translations.literal: Again, later scholars did not reach the former age, yet disputations clustered like stars, filling both sides of the page, spreading texts like brocade, brilliant and splendid to view.
translations.idiomatic: Later scholars did not match the ancients, yet disputations multiplied, pages overflowed, and prose spread like brocade—brilliant to behold.

sentences.zh: 然而五服之本或差，哀敬之制舛雜，國典未一于四海，家法參駁於縉紳，誠宜考詳遠慮，以定皇代之盛禮者也。

translations.literal: Yet the roots of the five garments of mourning sometimes differ, the regulations of grief and respect are mixed and confused, the national canon is not one throughout the four seas, and family law is at odds among the gentry—it is truly fitting to examine in detail with far-reaching thought and fix the splendid rites of the imperial age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the roots of mourning garments sometimes differ, grief and respect are inconsistently regulated, the national canon is not unified, and family law conflicts among the gentry—it is truly time to examine all with far-reaching care and fix the imperial age's full ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下欽明玄聖，同規唐、虞，疇咨四嶽，興言《三禮》，而伯夷未登，微臣竊位，所以大懼負乘，形神交惡者，無忘夙夜矣。

translations.literal: Bowingly considering that Your Majesty is reverent, bright, and mysteriously sage, matching the standards of Tang and Yu, consulting the four peaks, and raising discussion of the Three Rites—yet Bo Yi has not taken his post and your low servant holds office unworthily, therefore in great fear of the overloaded cart, body and spirit alike distressed, I dare not forget day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is reverent, luminous, and sage, matching Tang and Yu, consulting the four peaks, and raising the Three Rites—yet Bo Yi has not taken his post while I hold office unworthily; fearing the overloaded cart, body and spirit alike distressed, I dare not forget this day or night.

sentences.zh: 而複猥充搏采之數，與聞爰發之求，實無以仰酬聖旨萬分之一。

translations.literal: Yet again I am unworthily counted among those who gather and select, and heard the inquiry when it was first raised—I truly have no means to repay the sage command even one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am unworthily counted among those who gather materials and heard the inquiry at its start—I truly cannot repay your command even one part in ten thousand."

sentences.zh: 不敢廢默，謹率管穴所見五十二事上呈。

translations.literal: I dare not remain silent and respectfully present fifty-two matters seen through my narrow aperture.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not remain silent and respectfully submit fifty-two observations from my narrow learning.

sentences.zh: 蚩鄙茫浪，伏用竦赧。」

translations.literal: Ignorant, crude, and confused, I prostrate myself in fear and shame."
translations.idiomatic: Ignorant and crude, I prostrate myself in fear and shame."

sentences.zh: 明年，致仕，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired and received the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 歸老在家，手不釋卷，博學多通，特精《三禮》。

translations.literal: Returning to age at home, he never put down his scrolls; broadly learned and master of many fields, he was especially accomplished in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he never put down his books; erudite and widely learned, he was especially master of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 謹于奉公，常手抄書籍。

translations.literal: Diligent in serving the public, he often copied books by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent in public service, he often copied books by hand.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，時年八十三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died, at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：選賢於野，則治身業弘；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When worthies are chosen in the countryside, the work of self-cultivation flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: When worthies are chosen in the countryside, self-cultivation flourishes;

sentences.zh: 求士子朝，則飾智風起。

translations.literal: when scholars are sought at court, the wind of ornamented cleverness rises.
translations.idiomatic: when scholars are sought at court, the fashion of ornamented cleverness rises.

sentences.zh: 《六經》奧遠，方軌之正路；

translations.literal: The Six Classics are profound and far-reaching, the square track and correct road;
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics are profound and far-reaching—the true highway;

sentences.zh: 百家淺末，捷至之偏道。

translations.literal: the hundred schools shallow and marginal, the side path of quick arrival.
translations.idiomatic: the hundred schools shallow and marginal—a shortcut's side path.

sentences.zh: 漢世登士，閭黨為先，崇本務學，不尚浮詭，然後可以俯拾青組，顧蔑籝金。

translations.literal: In Han, men entered office with the village community first, honoring the root and devoting themselves to learning, not esteeming floating artifice—only then could they stoop to pick up blue cords and look down on casket gold.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, office began in the village community; men honored fundamentals and devoted themselves to study, not empty cleverness—only then could they gain office and scorn mere wealth.

sentences.zh: 於是人厲從師之志，家競專門之術，藝重當時，所居一旦成市，黌舍暫啟，著錄或至萬人。

translations.literal: Thus people sharpened the will to follow teachers, families competed in specialized arts, craft was weighty in the age—where one dwelt became a market in a day; when the schoolhouse briefly opened, registered students might reach ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Men sharpened their will to follow teachers; families competed in specialized arts; craft was prized—where a master lived became a market overnight, and when the schoolhouse opened, enrollment might reach ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 是故仕以學成，身由義立。

translations.literal: Therefore office came through learning completed, the person established through righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus office came through completed learning, and the person through established righteousness.

sentences.zh: 自魏氏膺命，主愛雕蟲，家棄章句，人重異術。

translations.literal: From the time Wei received the Mandate, rulers loved ornamental craft, families abandoned chapter-and-verse study, and men prized strange arts.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei received the Mandate, rulers loved ornamental prose, families abandoned classical glosses, and men prized strange arts.

sentences.zh: 又選賢進士，不本鄉閭，銓衡之寄，任歸台閣。

translations.literal: Again, in choosing worthies and advancing scholars, one did not take the village community as root; the charge of weighing and balancing was entrusted to the terrace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing worthies and advancing scholars no longer began in the village; weighing and selection rested with the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 以一人之耳目，究山川之險情，賢否臆斷，萬不值一。

translations.literal: With one man's eyes and ears to investigate the dangerous conditions of mountains and rivers, worth and unworth were judged by guess—not one in ten thousand was correct.
translations.idiomatic: With one man's eyes and ears to judge every corner of the realm, worth and unworth were guessed—hardly one judgment in ten thousand was right.

sentences.zh: 由是仕憑藉譽，學非為己，崇詭遇之巧速，鄙稅駕之遲難，士自此委笥植《經》，各從所務，早往晏退，以取世資。

translations.literal: Hence office relied on borrowed reputation, learning was not for oneself; they honored the clever speed of chance encounters and despised the slow difficulty of paying carriage tax; scholars from this time cast aside cases and planted the Classics only as each followed his business, going early and returning late to gain worldly capital.
translations.idiomatic: Office then relied on borrowed reputation; learning was not for oneself; men prized clever chance and despised slow thoroughness; scholars shelved their classics, each pursued his trade, hurried out and home late, and sought worldly gain.

sentences.zh: 庠序黌校之士，傳經聚徒之業，自黃初至於晉末，百餘年中，儒教盡矣。

translations.literal: The scholars of the schools and academies, the work of transmitting the classics and gathering disciples—from Huangchu to the end of Jin, more than a hundred years—Confucian teaching was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: School scholars and the work of transmitting classics and gathering disciples—from Huangchu to Jin's end, more than a century—Confucian teaching was spent.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，議創國學，宮車早晏，道未及行。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu received the Mandate, there was discussion of founding a National Academy, but the imperial carriage departed early and the Way was not yet carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu took the throne, a National Academy was proposed, but he died early and the plan was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 迄於元嘉，甫獲克就，雅風盛烈，未及曩時，而濟濟焉，頗有前王之遺典。

translations.literal: By Yuanjia it was at last achieved; elegant custom flourished grandly, not reaching the former age, yet in abundance—quite possessing the former kings' surviving canons.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanjia it was at last achieved; elegant learning flourished, though short of former ages, yet in abundance—with much of the former kings' ritual legacy restored.

sentences.zh: 天子鸞旗警蹕，清道而臨學館，儲後冕旒黼黻，北面而禮先師，後生所不嘗聞，黃發未之前睹，亦一代之盛也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven with imperial banners and cleared road came to the academy; the heir in cap and regalia faced north to honor the former master—what the young had never heard, what gray hair had never before seen: a splendor of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to the academy with banners flying and roads cleared; the heir in full regalia faced north to honor the former master—unheard by the young, unseen by the old: a splendor of the age.

sentences.zh: 臧燾、徐廣、傅隆、裴松之、何承天、雷次宗，並服膺聖哲，不為雅俗推移，立名於世，宜矣。

translations.literal: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all embraced the sages in their hearts and were not shifted by refined or vulgar fashion; to establish names in the world was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all embraced the sages and were not swayed by fashion; that they won lasting names was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 潁川庾蔚之、雁門周野王、汝南周王子、河內向琰、會稽賀道養，皆托志經書，見稱於後學。

translations.literal: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all set their aspirations in the classics and were praised by later students.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all devoted themselves to the classics and won praise from later scholars.

sentences.zh: 蔚之略解《禮記》，並注賀循《喪服》，行於世雲。

translations.literal: Weizhi had a partial understanding of the Record of Rites and also annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi had a partial grasp of the Record of Rites and annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments, both of which circulated widely.
